D.treatment: repurposed component and scripting mechanisms for plug-in tutors
D.comparison: broad, standardized deployment across application software

cells.quote: Both component systems and scripting systems proved too difficult to implement for application software developers, and the demand for them was too limited to support them in the form envisioned in the 1990s. More limited versions of systems like these still exist (for example, plug-in keyboards on A ndroid and IOS are examples of this type of component embedding; IOS also supports UI automation scripting through JavaScript and OS X ’s Automator has a recording facility at the user-interface level) but the vision that such systems would be fully implemented and standard across wide ranges of applications never came to pass.
cells.note: Narrative retrospective assessment; no learner sample, setting, duration, or quantitative effect is reported.

D.treatment: tool-tutor architecture in purpose-built instructional systems
D.comparison: plug-in tutors embedded in off-the-shelf software

cells.quote: However, the pedagogical approach assumed by the architecture remains relevant today, and the basics of the architecture are applicable in purpose-built instructional systems.
cells.note: The study distinguishes the unsuccessful broad off-the-shelf software vision from the continuing applicability of the separated tool-tutor architecture in purpose-built systems; this is a narrative claim, not a comparative learner outcome.
